title: No operator-drivable provisional capture client outside the harness agent loop
wanted_capability: A way to run one provisional capture (WorkspaceCaptureClient::sync_once) for a bound checkout from an operator command, so live validation of the provisional lane does not require dispatching a real LLM turn.
missing_primitive: A `bro workspace-binding capture` verb (or equivalent) that reads the three minted binding variables and drives one sync_once against the daemon.
fallback_used: Added crates/bbox-knowledge-source-client/examples/workspace-capture.rs, a public-API-only example performing the same construction the harness locality runtime does, and drove it from examples/graph-live-exercise.sh.
notes: Found while authoring the graph live exercise on branch feat/graph-live-exercise. The runbook already speaks of "a harness or capture client started with them", but only the harness agent loop constructs the client, so the provisional lane had no non-LLM live driver. Two adjacent defects surfaced in the same run and are described in examples/graph-live-exercise.md: the minted binding env file is not shell-sourceable (bare JSON scope value, while the runbook says to source it), and an own-visibility project graph read does not materialize the captured overlay until the bound session recomputes its own knowledge overlay pair.
resolution_note: bro workspace-binding capture shipped in the live-exercise fold (feat/graph-live-exercise @ 078f9b37, merged to beta/blackbox-v2): a thin operator verb wrapping the same WorkspaceCaptureClient construction the harness uses, reading the binding env file by default with flag and process-env overrides, refusing scope mismatches, never minting identity markers. Completes the operator loop: mint, edit, capture, query own visibility.
